EmergencyStopping and Stopping are both reachable leaves with zero outgoing transitions (LEAF_WITHOUT_OUTGOING), which raises stable-termination concerns for the NL10 retention contract and the NL2/NL3 endpoint contracts (endpoints exist, so no wrong-target issue, but termination-state ancestry needs review for EmergencyStopping since NL3 implies an active operating state with an entry action and an effect, not itself a formal completion, yet has no continuation at all -- this is dead-end, not the contract's own defect since NL3/EmergencyStopping is not typed termination_state; only Stopping might carry termination semantics but no explicit NL contract declares termination_state role here, so I do not fabricate a termination candidate). Event consumer coverage for Obstacle_Detected and Arrived_Stop_Send_Arrived are declared and reachable at Accelerating/Cruising/Approaching, satisfying event_consumer_coverage contract NL3-DERIVED. Root reachability: all 9 states reachable_from_initial=true per inspection_equivalent_facts, so no additional root-reachability derived contract is warranted. The distinctive behavioral defect is the malformed DoorsClosing-local initial edge to a synthetic InvalidInitialtr_0002 leaf (dead-end whose zero-outgoing fact is compiler-synthetic, so no separate deadlock candidate), which is already covered by the root/system init contract via the forced Closed_SendDeparted transition bypassing the malformed local edge -- I flag this against NL1-INIT-1 since though root->DoorsClosing exists, DoorsClosing's own nested initial-entry edge targets a synthetic invalid state, which is a distinct malformed nested edge fact worth noting under the same contract's exact owner scope only if it affects the DoorsClosing state itself; since NL1-INIT-1's owner is root/system targeting DoorsClosing (satisfied: tr_0001 root->DoorsClosing exists), that contract is satisfied and I omit it.
